newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra says Telstra may not maintain profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra says Telstra may not maintain profit.

text.p: Australian Communications Minister Richard Alston said government-owned telecommunciations carrier Telstra Corp might not be able to maintain the level of profitability announced earlier on Friday.

"You can't assume that these sorts of results will continue and indeed ... it will be a lot more competitive out there from July 1 next year," Alston told reporters after Telstra announced a A$2.3 billion net profit for the year to June 30.
"And inevitably that will put much greater pressure on Telstra, and Telstra management accept that," he said.

"They've been at pains to make it clear that they need to realise efficiency gains of some 30 percent, based on operating expenses per access line and in order to bring the company closer to world's best practise."

Alston had just reveAled the government's proposed system of telecommunications regulations to apply from July 1, when Telstra and rival Optus Communications Pty Ltd would lose their duopoly on most telecommunications services.
Under deregulation, anyone would have the right to install telecommunications infrastructure for their own use, but would require a licence in order to supply services to the public.

Earlier, Alston said plans to cut staff numbers at Telstra were the result of attempts to boost its competitiveness in the lead-up to deregulation, rather than a result of its planned partial sell-off.

The government plans to raise A$8.0 billion through the sale of one-third of Telstra. A non-government senate committee recommended against the sale earlier this week, saying it did not find any evidence that it would be beneficial.

The opposition Labor Party and the Australian Democrats both oppose the partial privatisation, leaving the fate of the Telstra bill in the hands of independent senators Brian Harradine and Mal Colston.
